thread.title: What to Watch: European stocks pop, Theresa May visits Brussels, oil prices bounce

author: uk.finance.yahoo.com
title: What to Watch: European stocks pop, Theresa May visits Brussels, oil prices bounce
text:
Here are the top business, market and economic stories you should be watching today in the UK, Europe and abroad:
European stocks defy gravity European stock markets were fairly buoyant on Wednesday, with Germany’s DAX ( ^GDAXI ) and Italy’s FTSE MIB ( FTSEMIB.MI ) up by roughly 1% in early trading.
Traders have grown hopeful that Italy could compromise with the European Commission over its contentious budget plans, which lifted Italian bank stocks. Investors have been worried about a damaging clash between the two sides.
Meanwhile, Asian markets ended the day with a mix of minor gains and losses.
This comes after US stocks plunged deep into negative territory on Tuesday. Apple ( AAPL ) was the biggest drag on the Dow Jones industrial average ( ^DJI ), as the index plummeted 551 points, sending it into the red on the year. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 1.8% on Tuesday and erased all of its year-to-date gains. The Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 1.7%. The tech-heavy index is down about 15% from its all-time highs.
US stock futures are indicating markets could bounce when trading resumes on Wednesday.
Theresa May visits Brussels for more Brexit talks British prime minister Theresa May arrives in Brussels on Wednesday to attempt to agree to a blueprint of Britain’s post-Brexit ties with the European Union. Disagreements remain over fisheries, trade and the disputed region of Gibraltar.
EU leaders are due to meet on Sunday to rubber-stamp the Brexit deal, which consists of Britain’s withdrawal agreement and a rough outline of plans for the new relationship between the two sides.
The fate of the withdrawal accord is uncertain, with deep reservations being expressed by parties on both sides.
Uncertainty about Brexit has sparked high volatility in the pound. It was trading around $1.28 against the US dollar ( GBPUSD=X ) and €1.12 against the euro ( GBPEUR=X ) in the early morning.
Market movers: Oil, Babcock and Johnson Matthey Crude oil prices bounced back on Wednesday morning after enduring a sharp drop on Tuesday. WTI crude futures ( CL=F ) and Brent prices ( BZ=F ) were rising by about 1% to 2%, lifted by a report of an unexpected decline in US commercial crude inventories and record Indian crude imports.
WTI crude oil futures are now trading around $54.50 per barrel, down by nearly 30% from early October when the price was about $76.50 per barrel.
Corporate updates have triggered some sharp share price moves on Wednesday. Babcock ( BAB.L ) stock plummeted by as much as 12% in London after the British defence contractor took a one-off charge of £120m ($153m) to reshape its business and warned that revenue from its nuclear decommissioning division would drop by more than expected.
Johnson Matthey ( JMAT.L ) was among the main gainers in Europe after rising by 8% in morning trading. Investors were feeling bullish after the specialty chemicals company raised its full-year guidance.
Patisserie Valerie: New investigation The UK’s Financial Reporting Council has launched an investigation into Grant Thornton UK over its audit of Patisserie Holdings ( CAKE.L ), the owner of the Patisserie Valerie chain.
Patisserie Holdings was recently rocked by an accounting scandal and came close to collapse before getting a £20m ($26m) lifeline from chairman Luke Johnson.
The accounting watchdog, which sets UK standards for accounting, said it would examine three years of Patisserie Holdings’ financial statements.
With files from Reuters and Yahoo Finance’s Heidi Chung
